releaseOwner.note: Not approved. The engineering gates below were observed passing and are recorded as evidence, but a release-owner approval is a human attestation and has not been given for 1.1.0. `pnpm validate:public-release-approval --tag v1.1.0` fails until the owner fills in name and approvedAt themselves.

licenceCompliance.note: `pnpm validate:licenses` passes and is recorded, but NOTICE review is a human reading task and has not been repeated for 1.1.0. This release adds no new runtime dependency; if the terminal-UI pixel font is vendored before the tag, its OFL attribution must be added to NOTICE and reviewed here.

deferredChannels.reason: No Apple Developer ID or Windows signing certificate has been procured, so no notarized DMG, signed MSI, deb or AppImage exists. The native release policy still requires a verified upgrade from an older signed installer before any stable native artifact ships.
The Tauri updater channel depends on signed native artifacts and is deferred with them.
Packages are version-locked and pack cleanly, but publication requires the maintainer's npm account and GitHub Actions OIDC on the canonical tag workflow.

The console ships with inline SVG stand-ins for all 37 sprites and the platform monospace stack. The generated pixel art and the vendored OFL pixel font are tracked in docs/design/codex-image-generation-packet.md and are a visual upgrade, not a functional gate.

notes: 1.1.0 is additive: the nine-tool workflow registry, the REST surface it already published, the SDK, the CLI and the .marketingovo bundle format are unchanged. It adds ten agent-session REST routes, a separate five-tool terminal session registry, a client.terminal SDK surface, and the console dashboard.

The packaged browser journey did not pass on the branch before this release preparation: it navigated through a sidebar entry the monorepo consolidation had already removed. Fixing it surfaced eleven pre-existing WCAG AA contrast failures and two undefined design tokens, all repaired here.
This record covers the source, CLI, MCP plugin and npm-packable surfaces. It deliberately does not claim any signed native artifact, and it deliberately does not claim an approval nobody gave.
